item.text: {"rubric":[{"claim_id":"c1","claim_type":"core","weight":20,"statement":"The answer uses the ordinary synchronous `Evaluate(...)(program)` path, matching that `Evaluate.__call__` is a regular method and runs evaluation work through `ParallelExecutor` rather than an async entrypoint.","span_ids":["s1","s2"]},{"claim_id":"c2","claim_type":"core","weight":40,"statement":"It shows that per-example scoring is performed synchronously: DSPy computes the prediction and then calls `metric(example, prediction)` directly with no `await`, so passing an `async def` metric yields a coroutine object as the score.","span_ids":["s2"]},{"claim_id":"c3","claim_type":"core","weight":30,"statement":"It identifies the failure site in the sync evaluator: DSPy aggregates scores with `sum(score for *_, score in results)`, so coroutine scores produce a `TypeError` about unsupported operand types that mentions a coroutine.","span_ids":["s3"]},{"claim_id":"c4","claim_type":"supporting","weight":10,"statement":"It treats the sync evaluation as expected to raise before a normal `EvaluationResult(score=..., results=...)` can be constructed, so the repro should catch and assert the exception instead of expecting a successful evaluation result.","span_ids":["s3","s4","s5"]}],"evidence":[{"span_id":"s1","path":"dspy/evaluate/evaluate.py","start_line":116,"end_line":128},{"span_id":"s2","path":"dspy/evaluate/evaluate.py","start_line":162,"end_line":175},{"span_id":"s3","path":"dspy/evaluate/evaluate.py","start_line":178,"end_line":182},{"span_id":"s4","path":"dspy/evaluate/evaluate.py","start_line":223,"end_line":226},{"span_id":"s5","path":"dspy/evaluate/evaluate.py","start_line":57,"end_line":58}]}
